name: Fox Corporation (Class B)
key_signal: FOX trades at just 9.5x forward earnings and has shown a sharp positive momentum reversal (21d +7.7%, MACD turning positive) even though the stock remains below its 50/200-day averages after a tough comp against last year's election-cycle ad boom.
thesis: At a forward P/E of 9.5x and price-to-book under 2x, FOX is priced for permanent decline despite still generating 21.4% operating margins, 15.2% ROE, and $1.4B in free cash flow on $16.2B revenue. The -8.6% revenue growth and -49.3% earnings growth almost certainly reflect a tough year-over-year comparison against 2024's outsized political and NFL-cycle ad revenue rather than structural deterioration, and low beta (0.55) plus a 1.08% dividend suggest the market already treats this as a defensive, mature cash-generator. The recent 21-day +7.7% bounce, positive 1-day return, and MACD histogram turning sharply positive (0.76) suggest the multi-month downtrend (-21.6% over 126 days) may be stabilizing as the stock sits near its 52-week low ($44.08) with room to $68 highs.
bear_case: The stock is below both its 50-day ($53.82) and 200-day ($56.62) moving averages with no golden cross, confirming the intermediate trend remains bearish, and a -49.3% earnings decline plus -8.6% revenue growth are not merely cyclical noise but evidence that linear cord-cutting and audience erosion at Fox News and cable are structurally impairing the base business even as debt-to-equity sits elevated at 67.9%; if the political/NFL comp explanation is wrong and margins keep compressing, the 'cheap' multiple is a value trap, and 57% annualized volatility shows the market is already pricing real downside risk rather than an anomaly.
